title: The Bigger Picture — Daily AI Analysis
paragraphs: A deeper look at today's Bigger Picture card: what is moving the market, and what to watch. The Full Report carries the full analysis.

What moves the market today. Fact: Reuters reports, citing a person familiar with the matter, that OpenAI told investors its yearly revenue pace for September was almost $50 billion, not the roughly $70 billion it had signalled, mainly because of a counting difference: Anthropic counts sales through cloud partners, OpenAI does not. Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that OpenAI still expects a $70 billion pace by the end of 2026 while seeking $30 billion or more at a $1.4 trillion value. Reuters reports that SoftBank, a major OpenAI investor, fell 5.4% in early trading after the report, with bond stress and oil also weighing.

Fact: Reuters reports that Firmus, an Nvidia-backed Australian data-centre builder, shelved its $5 billion share sale after investors pulled orders over its debt, its short record and a price near triple its August value; a fund manager quoted by Reuters called it "an important reality check", not the end of the AI boom. Bloomberg reports that Oracle, Broadcom, SpaceX and others have sold nearly half a trillion dollars of new debt this year for AI, and that insuring Oracle's and Broadcom's debt against default now costs a record; those are market prices, not predictions.

Our view: the market is starting to pay for proof, not plans. A $20 billion counting change was followed by a 5% fall in a major backer's shares, a sign of thin information under the biggest valuations, while a builder with heavy debt and a short record shelved its share sale. Memory is getting dearer and a major optical supplier says it is sold out, so building costs more as borrowing does.

What to watch and follow. 1. Whether OpenAI's round closes at $1.4 trillion and with which revenue definition, and whether Firmus finds private money: together they say if the reality check is one company's or the sector's. 2. The price of the next Oracle, Broadcom or SpaceX debt sale: nearly half a trillion dollars of this year's build is borrowed. 3. Memory and optical supply, with Chinese chip prices reported up 20% to 50% and Lumentum's chief executive saying it is sold out to 2029: the cost of every new data centre.
